purpose: Declared-failure ledger for `python scripts/check_forecast_invariants.py --sidecar-dir` (CI job `forecast-invariant-artifacts`, added by FFR-1D for audit finding FR-24). Every FAIL recorded in a committed run sidecar under frontend/data/hindcast/ must appear here, so a NEWLY registered run that fails an invariant is a reviewed line in this file rather than a number that lands on the forecast dashboard unremarked. Adding a line is not absolution: an invariant FAIL is a root-cause finding (rules 1/11), and the open ones are tracked in docs/forecast-readiness-audit-2026-07.md.
how_to_update: Registering a run whose sidecar carries a FAIL: add `"<run_id>": ["I4", ...]` below in the same commit as the registration, and name the finding it belongs to in your findings doc. Removing a run's sidecar, or fixing the defect so the invariant passes, means DELETING its line here — the checker fails on a stale declaration too.

dominant_open_causes.I3: unserved/dump — NOT one cause, and NOT ERCOT-only (corrected 2026-08-31, lane capx D-18). IN ERCOT the slack leg is FR-6: the adequacy backstop is disabled for energy-only ERCOT by market design (`resolve_reserve_margin_build_enabled` returns False; `capacity_evolution/adequacy.py`), so a one-pass under-build has no corrective and lands as LP slack at VOLL — structural and unowned in code, magnitude comparable only within a solve vintage (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d4i3-ercot-slack-2026-08-31.md §§2/5.1). OUTSIDE ERCOT FR-6 CANNOT BE THE CAUSE: MISO and NEISO are capacity-market ISOs where the same resolver returns True and the backstop IS armed, so their I3 rows are a different mechanism — miso-2026-2030-s123-verify is a slack breach (2029/2030) whose measured chain is FINDING-capx-s123-miso-adequacy-2026-08-30.md §5, and neiso-2026-2050-t3-golden-bau trips the OTHER leg of the invariant entirely, out-year renewable DUMP rising 2.17 %→8.50 % of renewable potential 2043-2050 (FINDING-capx-t3-neiso-golden-2026-08-30.md §6.3(2)). What actually drives each is OPEN and belongs to that ISO's own lane (rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]); this line names the question and deliberately does not answer it.

post_clear_note: 2026-08-19: first post-clear registration. pjm-2021-2025-realized-k162 (T1-H plain hindcast 2021-2025 on the current PJM keeper 2026-08-15-pjm-162-inputclock) carries I7 — 2025 accredited firm 138,785 MW vs a 139,850 MW requirement, a 1,065 MW / 0.76 % shortfall. THIS IS NOT THE FR-3 HYDRO CAUSE listed in dominant_open_causes: PJM hydro IS accredited in this run (firm_clean_accredited_mw 1,254 MW of 3,301 MW LP nameplate). The cause is upstream, in the retirement ledger, and it is the harness working as designed rather than a defect. The 2022 bridge-year evolution retires 4,097 MW of nuclear on reason='announced' — Byron 1+2 (plant 6023) and Dresden 2+3 (plant 869), whose 2020-vintage EIA-860 rows carry Exelon's 2020-08-27 PJM deactivation dates. Illinois CEJA (P.A. 102-0662) reversed both on 2021-09-15, so PJM actually retired 0 GW of nuclear in the window; but the RC-1B information gate in data.confirmed_retirements.load_announced_reversal_plants keys the reversal on superseding_instrument_date (2021-09-15) against this run's 2020-12-31 vintage cutoff, and therefore correctly declines to suppress the announced exit — its own docstring names this exact case. A forecaster standing at end-2020 would have retired both plants. That 4,097 MW of removed firm nuclear is ~3.8x the I7 shortfall and is also 62 % of the run's 6.645 GW false-retire total, so the I7 FAIL, the false-retire FAIL and the +13 % thermal-retire band miss share this one cause. Declared, NOT absolution, and no band or threshold was touched (rules 1/11/14).
